skill.name: wp-docker
skill.description: Create local WordPress development environments with Docker Compose, MariaDB, WP-CLI, and setup templates.
skill.summary: Creates repeatable local WordPress Docker environments with WP-CLI setup automation.
skill.author: CrazySwami

security_audit.summary: The skill is a legitimate WordPress development helper, but it intentionally uses Docker Compose, WP-CLI, filesystem templates, and a Bash setup script. Most Markdown backtick and role-token findings are false positives, while weak default credentials, destructive Docker operations, and credential display require remediation. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Remove sample passwords and require users to provide strong WordPress administrator, database, and root database passwords before setup runs.
Do not echo the administrator password after setup. Print only the username and login URL.
Require explicit confirmation and a recent backup before volume removal, database import, search-replace, or cache reset commands.
Have the assistant present planned Docker and WP-CLI commands for review before running Bash actions.

remediation.issue: Resolved environment values can appear in output
remediation.suggestion: Warn users that docker-compose config can display secrets, and avoid sharing its full output.

semantic_findings.title: Weak Default WordPress Administrator Passwords
semantic_findings.description: The quick start uses the sample administrator password password, and the setup script falls back to password123. Users may expose a WordPress admin account if they run these defaults.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The sample and default admin passwords are directly visible in the documented setup path. They are weak credentials for any site reachable beyond a private local machine.

semantic_findings.title: Setup Script Prints Administrator Password
semantic_findings.description: The setup script prints the administrator password at completion. This can expose credentials in terminal scrollback, shared session logs, or captured build output.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The script explicitly echoes the password variable after setup. This is a direct local disclosure risk even when the password was supplied by the user.

content.value_statement: Local WordPress setup can be slow when containers, databases, and WP-CLI steps are repeated by hand. This skill provides Docker Compose templates and setup guidance for repeatable development sites.
actual_capabilities: Create a Docker Compose stack with MariaDB, WordPress, and WP-CLI services.
Copy template files for compose, PHP upload limits, and site setup.
Install WordPress core with supplied site URL, title, and admin credentials.
Install and activate common WordPress plugins through WP-CLI.
Run WP-CLI workflows for pages, permalinks, migrations, and plugin audits.
Configure PHP upload, memory, and execution limits for development.
limitations: It targets local development and does not harden production hosting.
It depends on Docker Compose, WordPress images, and internet access for plugin installs.
It uses default credentials unless users supply stronger values.
It does not replace backup, security review, or deployment approval steps.

use_cases.title: Start Client Site Sandboxes
use_cases.description: Create repeatable local WordPress projects with containers, WP-CLI setup, and starter pages.

use_cases.title: Standardize Agency Development
use_cases.description: Give team members the same Docker stack, plugin baseline, PHP limits, and troubleshooting commands.

use_cases.title: Test Site Changes Locally
use_cases.description: Import content, update URLs, verify plugins, and test configuration changes before production work.

prompt_templates.title: Create a New Local Site
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a fresh project
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the wp-docker skill to prepare a new local WordPress site. Show the files needed, ask for passwords, and wait before running commands.

prompt_templates.title: Review the Docker Stack
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the wp-docker templates and summarize the services, volumes, ports, environment variables, and security changes I should make first.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Local Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Use wp-docker to plan a local migration from an existing WordPress backup. Include backup checks, import order, URL replacement, and rollback points.

prompt_templates.title: Audit and Harden the Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my wp-docker setup for unsafe defaults, exposed secrets, destructive commands, and production risks. Give prioritized fixes before any shell action.

output_examples.input: Create a local WordPress site for a brochure project.
output_examples.output: A setup plan with required template files, Docker services to start, requested credentials, and the first pages to create.

output_examples.input: Check whether my Docker WordPress stack is ready.
output_examples.output: A readiness review covering container status, database health, WordPress installation state, mounted content, and next safe commands.

output_examples.input: Prepare a safe local migration test.
output_examples.output: A migration checklist with backup confirmation, database import steps, URL replacement scope, plugin checks, and rollback guidance.

best_practices: Replace default admin and database passwords before running the setup script.
Review generated Docker and WP-CLI commands before allowing shell execution.
Keep local backups before imports, search-replace operations, or volume removal.
anti_patterns: Do not reuse the sample password or database defaults on exposed hosts.
Do not run destructive Docker volume commands without a recent backup.
Do not treat the local stack as a production deployment.

faq.question: Does this skill create a production WordPress host?
faq.answer: No. It is designed for local development and testing with Docker Compose.

faq.question: Which tools does it expect?
faq.answer: It expects Docker Compose and access to WordPress container images and WP-CLI commands.

faq.question: Can it install plugins automatically?
faq.answer: Yes. The setup script installs a defined plugin set through WP-CLI when approved.

faq.question: Should I keep the default passwords?
faq.answer: No. Replace all sample passwords before running setup or exposing the site.

faq.question: Can it help with migrations?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents database export, import, URL replacement, and cache flush workflows.

faq.question: Does it require internet access?
faq.answer: Yes for pulling images and installing WordPress plugins or themes from remote sources.
